decisions.reason: Only a brief website mention suggests lower public commitment, but the recent product-line investment and sunk engineering costs still argue against dropping it within a year.

Its dedicated product page reflects visible commitment and the spring-balanced desk lamp has enough sunk development costs to make near-term withdrawal unlikely despite its weaker fit with the announced smart-lighting direction.
As a core general interior luminaire with its own page and an active model launch, it is central to the firm's announced direction and carries high sunk investment, making a quick drop very unlikely.

As the publicly presented flagship with high centrality to the announced sustainable and intelligent lighting direction, dropping it within the next year would contradict the firm's strong commitment and sunk resources.

The marine HMI searchlight is only briefly mentioned and sits outside the core LED/human-centric direction, so commitment is thinner, but the recent launch and sunk costs still make a near-term drop less likely than keeping it.

Similar to the HMI searchlight, this marine searchlight has low public visibility and weaker alignment with the announced direction, yet sunk costs and the need to justify the 2023 launch keep it on the market for now.
